analysis.title: US EQUITIES - a pulse check
key_insights: The S&P 500 fell less than 50bps on the week and sits 2.5% below its highs, but hedge fund portfolios took heavy losses below the index surface.

On Thursday, all three major hedge fund cohorts (Fundamental L/S, Systematic, Multi-Strats) lost more than 1% on the same day for the first time since COVID. The GS Hedge Fund VIP long/short basket fell 4%, a move only matched over the past decade by DeepSeek Monday and the COVID selloff.
TMT-focused hedge funds are down 9.6% month to date and Asia Fundamental L/S is down 9.3% month to date.
The desk reads this as an investor leverage unwind rather than an AI demand bubble bursting. Positioning has moved much faster than AI fundamentals.

Hedge fund gross leverage still stood at 312% (96th percentile over five years) after the selling, while fundamental net leverage fell to 47%, a one-year low. Funds became more defensive without working down gross exposure, which explains the persistent pain.

The GS floor saw about $20bn of TMT selling over two weeks, approaching the $23bn seen during July's AI unwind. The moves in the most crowded parts of the market are almost identical to July, but SPX is down 2.4% this time versus 3.4% in July.
AI stocks are moving together more closely while index volatility stays relatively contained. The desk hopes the market is nearing a better positioning equilibrium, as it did after July.

The risk is that discretionary selling gives way to systematic selling. CTAs are long $38.5bn of S&P futures (91st percentile), about 80% of aggregate net longs across the 21 markets tracked. The S&P is already below its short-term trend threshold and the medium-term level is about 1.3% below Friday's close.

Modeled CTA flows are asymmetric: an estimated $11.6bn of S&P selling over the next week in a flat tape and up to $65bn in a one-month downside scenario, versus only $9bn of buying in a one-month upside scenario. Even a 2 SD rally next week leaves CTAs net sellers.
Nasdaq CTA signals have deteriorated, while Russell CTA positioning is heavily short and could force buying on a rally.

SPX volatility is starting to react: fixed-strike vol is bid, downside skew and tails are outperforming, and VIX positioning (particularly VIX volatility) is drawing attention. The Vol Panic Index rose from 4.63 Wednesday to 7.94 Friday, reaching the 'panic' threshold for the first time since late July.

Catalysts this week: Microsoft and Alphabet report Wednesday along with the Fed decision, and Amazon reports Thursday. Earnings matter more after META given scrutiny of AI capex, funding needs and returns. Strong results could stabilize sentiment but the bar for reassurance has risen.

The desk flags Korea after a 40% KOSPI correction. GS research cut its 12-month target from 12,000 to 9,000 but still sees more than 60% upside, with KOSPI at 4x forward earnings pricing in bad news on the memory cycle.
Brazil is in focus after the presidential runoff, with EWZ, the currency and local rates offering opportunities different from the crowded AI trade.

The author's bias is a relief rally after two weeks of selling, held loosely given elevated gross exposure, negative systematic flow asymmetry and geopolitical wildcards. The desk favors call spreads to express upside with defined downside.
